denomProfiles/old-catholic/tagline: Catholic churches of the first millennium, independent of Rome since 1870.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/coreDoctrines: Faith of the undivided church of the first millennium and the seven ecumenical councils (Declaration of Utrecht, 1889).
Rejection of papal infallibility and universal jurisdiction as defined at Vatican I (1870).
Rejection of the dogma of the Immaculate Conception (1854) as lacking ancient warrant.
Seven sacraments; Christ truly present in the Eucharist, without binding definition of transubstantiation.
Autonomous national churches united in a synodal communion of bishops.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/focuses/0: Catholic order with synodal governance including clergy and laity.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/focuses/1: Ecumenism, especially full communion with Anglicans (Bonn Agreement, 1931).
denomProfiles/old-catholic/focuses/2: Liturgy in the vernacular, adopted from the 1870s onwards.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/focuses/3: Inclusion: women ordained as priests (Germany from 1996) and in some churches as bishops.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/practices/0: Eucharist in a revised Western Catholic liturgy in German, Dutch and other languages.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/practices/3: General confession in the liturgy; private confession optional.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/practices/4: Blessing of same-sex unions in several member churches.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/influenced/0/: Bonn Agreement of 1931 brought full communion with the Church of England.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/influenced/1/: A member of the Union of Utrecht from 1907 to 2003.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/influenced/2/: In full communion with the Union of Utrecht since 1965.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/influenced/3/: Many 'independent' bishops trace their orders to Old Catholic consecrations.
denomProfiles/old-catholic/keyFigures/0/: Historian excommunicated in 1871 for rejecting infallibility
denomProfiles/old-catholic/keyFigures/1/: First Old Catholic bishop in Germany (1873)
denomProfiles/old-catholic/keyFigures/2/: First bishop of the Christian Catholic Church of Switzerland (1876)
denomProfiles/old-catholic/keyFigures/3/: Archbishop of Utrecht consecrated without papal approval in 1724
denomProfiles/chaldean-catholic/tagline: East Syriac church of Iraq in communion with Rome since 1553.
denomProfiles/chaldean-catholic/coreDoct: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
East Syriac theological heritage of the Church of the East, reconciled with Catholic doctrine.
Christ one person in two natures; the 1994 Catholic–Assyrian declaration recognised shared faith in Christ.
Validity of the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, which lacks explicit words of institution (Rome, 2001).
denomProfiles/chaldean-catholic/focuses/: Survival and return of Christians in Iraq after war and the Islamic State's 2014 expulsions.
Preservation of Syriac (Sureth) language and liturgy.
A large diaspora in the United States, Australia, Europe and Canada.
Christian–Muslim relations in Iraq, highlighted by Pope Francis' visit in 2021.
denomProfiles/chaldean-catholic/practice: Holy Qurbana of Addai and Mari in Syriac, Arabic and modern Aramaic.
East Syriac liturgical year, including the Rogation of the Ninevites.
Married priests in the Middle East.
Patriarch of Babylon of the Chaldeans resident in Baghdad.
denomProfiles/chaldean-catholic/influenc: Shared heritage led to joint guidelines on mutual admission to the Eucharist (2001).
Chaldean prelates oversaw the Kerala St Thomas Christians in the 16th and 19th centuries.
denomProfiles/chaldean-catholic/keyFigur: First patriarch in union with Rome, martyred in 1555
Patriarch 1848–78 who resisted Latinisation at Vatican I
denomProfiles/chaldean-catholic/members/: CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017 (statistical table compiled from the Annuario Pontificio).
denomProfiles/chaldean-catholic/inIndia: There is no Chaldean eparchy in India, but Chaldean bishops served the St Thomas Christians in the 16th century, and the 1874 mission of Mar Elias Mellus at Thrissur led to the Chaldean Syrian Church, now part of the Assyrian Church of the East.
denomProfiles/maronite-catholic/tagline: Lebanon's Syriac Catholic church of St Maron, never separated from Rome by its own account.
denomProfiles/maronite-catholic/coreDoct: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Antiochene Syriac theological heritage, with strong Latin influence since the 16th century.
Maronite tradition of 'perpetual orthodoxy' and continuous communion with Rome, which some historians question for the 7th–12th centuries.
Veneration of saints of the Lebanese mountains, such as Charbel Makhlouf (canonised 1977).
denomProfiles/maronite-catholic/focuses/: Lebanese national and Christian identity since the Ottoman and French mandate periods.
Monastic life of the Lebanese orders in the mountains.
Education, through institutions such as Université Saint-Esprit de Kaslik.
A diaspora larger than the home community, in the Americas and Australia.
denomProfiles/maronite-catholic/practice: Qurbono (Divine Liturgy) of West Syriac origin in Arabic, with Syriac chants such as the Qadishat.
Anaphora of the Twelve Apostles and other Syriac anaphoras.
Married priests in Lebanon and, since 2014, permitted in the diaspora.
Pilgrimage to the Qadisha Valley, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
denomProfiles/maronite-catholic/influenc: Maronite Lebanon gave refuge to other Eastern Catholic communities.
Maronite scholars such as the Assemani family brought Syriac learning to Europe.
The National Pact of 1943 reserved the presidency of Lebanon for a Maronite.
denomProfiles/maronite-catholic/keyFigur: Syrian hermit (d. c. 410), patron of the church
Patriarch 1670–1704 and historian of the church
Patriarch of Antioch since 2011 and cardinal
denomProfiles/maronite-catholic/members/: CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017 (statistical table compiled from the Annuario Pontificio).
denomProfiles/melkite-greek-catholic/tag: Arabic-speaking Byzantine Catholic church of Antioch, Damascus and the Levant.
denomProfiles/melkite-greek-catholic/cor: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Byzantine Orthodox theology and spirituality held together with communion with Rome.
A strong theology of the local church and synod, defended at Vatican I and Vatican II.
Hope for reunion with the Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch, from which it separated in 1724.
denomProfiles/melkite-greek-catholic/foc: Christian presence and schools in Syria, Lebanon, Israel–Palestine and Jordan.
Ecumenism with the Antiochian Orthodox Church.
Diaspora communities in the Americas and Australia.
denomProfiles/melkite-greek-catholic/pra: Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom in Arabic and Greek.
Icons, Byzantine hymnody and Eastern fasting.
Married priests, including in the diaspora.
Infant initiation by baptism, chrismation and first communion together.
denomProfiles/melkite-greek-catholic/inf: Patriarch Maximos IV Sayegh pressed for the vernacular, collegiality and Eastern dignity.
Archbishop Elias Zoghby proposed communion with both Rome and Orthodoxy.
A leading voice for de-Latinisation among Eastern Catholics.
denomProfiles/melkite-greek-catholic/key: Patriarch who secured Ottoman civil recognition (1848)
Patriarch who opposed infallibility at Vatican I
Patriarch and cardinal, voice of the East at Vatican II
denomProfiles/melkite-greek-catholic/mem: CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017 (statistical table compiled from the Annuario Pontificio).
denomProfiles/ukrainian-greek-catholic/t: Largest Eastern Catholic church, heir of Kyivan Christianity and the 1596 Union of Brest.
denomProfiles/ukrainian-greek-catholic/c: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Kyivan Byzantine heritage dating from the baptism of Rus' (988).
Union with Rome on the terms of the Union of Brest (1595–96), retaining Eastern rite and married clergy.
Self-understanding as a patriarchal church, though Rome recognises a major archbishopric.
denomProfiles/ukrainian-greek-catholic/f: Ukrainian national and civic life, especially in western Ukraine.
Memory of martyrs under Soviet persecution after the forced 'liquidation' at the 1946 Lviv pseudo-synod.
Humanitarian aid and pastoral care during the Russian invasion since 2022.
Education through the Ukrainian Catholic University in Lviv.
Diaspora churches in Canada, the United States, Brazil and Argentina.
denomProfiles/ukrainian-greek-catholic/p: Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom in Ukrainian and Church Slavonic.
Icons and iconostasis, Byzantine chant and Eastern feasts, mostly on the Revised Julian calendar since 2023.
Married priests are the norm in Ukraine.
Underground worship in homes and forests during the Soviet ban (1946–89).
denomProfiles/ukrainian-greek-catholic/i: The neighbouring Union of Uzhhorod (1646) followed the Brest model.
Ukrainian church life after 1989 shaped the push for an independent Orthodox church.
Its revival after 1989 became a sore point with the Moscow Patriarchate.
denomProfiles/ukrainian-greek-catholic/k: Archbishop of Polotsk killed in 1623, venerated as a saint
Metropolitan 1901–44 who sheltered Jews in the Holocaust
Head of the church imprisoned 18 years in the Gulag
Major Archbishop 2001–11 who moved the see to Kyiv (2005)
denomProfiles/ukrainian-greek-catholic/m: CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017 (statistical table compiled from the Annuario Pontificio).
denomProfiles/syro-malabar-catholic/tagl: Kerala's St Thomas Christians in communion with Rome, East Syriac in liturgy.
denomProfiles/syro-malabar-catholic/core: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Apostolic origin from St Thomas, who by tradition landed at Kodungallur (Muziris) in AD 52.
East Syriac theological and liturgical heritage received from the Church of the East.
Self-governing major archiepiscopal church with its own synod (since 1992).
denomProfiles/syro-malabar-catholic/focu: Very high numbers of priestly and religious vocations, serving across India and worldwide.
Schools, colleges and hospitals throughout Kerala.
Recovery of Syriac identity after centuries of Latinisation.
Mission dioceses in north India and a growing diaspora.
The dispute over the mode of celebrating the Qurbana, especially in Ernakulam–Angamaly.
denomProfiles/syro-malabar-catholic/prac: Holy Qurbana of Addai and Mari in Malayalam, with Syriac elements.
Synod-mandated 'uniform' Qurbana since 2021: facing the people for the liturgy of the Word, facing the altar for the anaphora.
Lenten fasting, Passover meal (Pesaha) customs on Maundy Thursday, and the Mar Thoma cross.
Pilgrimage to Thomas sites such as Malayattoor and to the tomb of St Alphonsa at Bharananganam.
denomProfiles/syro-malabar-catholic/infl: Those who left Roman jurisdiction after the Coonan Cross Oath (1653) formed the Malankara churches.
A second St Thomas Christian Catholic church formed in 1930.
Syro-Malabar priests and nuns serve in Latin dioceses across India and abroad.
denomProfiles/syro-malabar-catholic/keyF: Traditional founder of Christianity in India
Founder of the CMI congregation and educator, canonised 2014
Franciscan Clarist, first Indian woman saint (2008)
denomProfiles/syro-malabar-catholic/memb: CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017 (statistical table compiled from the Annuario Pontificio).
denomProfiles/syro-malabar-catholic/inIn: Centred in central Kerala (Ernakulam, Thrissur, Kottayam, Changanassery), with eparchies across India including Thuckalay and Ramanathapuram in Tamil Nadu and a nationwide jurisdiction since 2017; it is the second-largest Eastern Catholic church in the world.
